title: Control flow and decisions
summary: Use conditionals and loops to transform collections of values.

scenario.briefing: The advising report includes every task, including incomplete ones. Write a function that returns only completed task titles.

hints: Return a new array; do not mutate the input.
Use const result = []; for (const task of tasks) { if (task.done) result.push(task.title); } return result;

misconceptions.testDescription: Does not mutate the input array.
misconceptions.feedback: Do not mutate the caller's data. Build and return a new array.

misconceptions.description: Confusing truthy values with strict true.
misconceptions.feedback: JavaScript coerces values in conditionals. Use strict checks when the distinction matters.

sections.title: Conditionals
sections.body: if selects a branch based on a condition. Strict equality === avoids type coercion. A condition can be any expression, but relying on truthiness can hide bugs.

sections.title: Loops
sections.body: for...of iterates over iterable values. Build new arrays instead of mutating inputs to keep functions predictable.
